scope: OMSI manufacturing semantic validator, replay envelope, and future Mycelix receipt adapter
principles: Correctness and safety invariants are hard gates; performance cannot compensate for a semantic or privacy failure.
Queued CI and historical results are not exact-head passes.
Performance targets are provisional until measured on a named reference host with a sufficiently representative corpus.
No score or benchmark result confers product-release, machine-control, calibration-authentication, or safety authority.

gates.acceptance: Every committed expected outcome must match the evaluator exactly for the versioned fields.
gates.failure_policy: Block release; never weaken a negative vector merely to obtain a pass.

gates.acceptance: No cross-tenant input, malformed decimal/time, incompatible unit, missing required metadata, or contradictory source claim may be optimistically accepted.
gates.failure_policy: Block release and preserve the failing minimized fixture.

gates.acceptance: All success, reject, conflict, loss and replay-verification reports validate with an independent JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 implementation; mutated reports are rejected.
gates.failure_policy: Block release; serde parsing is not a substitute for JSON Schema validation.

gates.acceptance: Detect every catalogued mutation to exact input bytes, digest, envelope contract, required limitations and embedded semantic report.
gates.failure_policy: Block release; unsigned digest binding must not be described as source authentication.

gates.acceptance: Same input bytes, profile/rule versions and validator build produce semantically equal reports across repeated runs.
gates.failure_policy: Block release and retain corpus digest, build identity and differing fields.

gates.acceptance: Exercise decimal boundaries, timezone equivalence, malformed inputs, scope isolation and evidence monotonicity using reproducible seeds; a separate minimized regression fixture is committed for every found defect.
gates.failure_policy: Do not promote beyond incubation until the test generator, seed and results are reproducible.

gates.acceptance: Fuzz parsing, profile-shape, decimal/time fields and envelope verification under resource limits; store corpus and crash artifacts.
gates.failure_policy: Any crash, panic, uncontrolled allocation or inconsistent acceptance blocks promotion until triaged.

gates.workload: Single synthetic observation input <= 32 KiB; at least 1000 representative cases; pinned release build and named reference host.
gates.acceptance: Report p50/p95/p99 and host/compiler metadata over repeated independent runs. Do not gate shared GitHub-hosted CI on timing until the environment is controlled.
gates.failure_policy: Profile before optimizing; never trade away semantic checks for throughput.

gates.workload: Input artifact <= 64 KiB; report replay includes digest, parsing and fresh semantic evaluation.
gates.acceptance: Measure on the same pinned reference host as semantic evaluation.
gates.failure_policy: Profile hashing, parsing and evaluation separately; do not skip verification steps.

gates.workload: At least 1000 representative cases across valid, reject, loss and conflict outcomes.
gates.acceptance: Use the phase wall_clock_operations_per_second and wall_clock_serialized_input_mib_per_second fields measured over the full phase batch. Keep sampled-time rates as inverse-mean-latency equivalents; they must not substitute for measured wall-clock throughput. Record corpus digest, input-size distribution, compiler profile, CPU, OS and run count.
gates.failure_policy: A throughput result is not comparable without matching workload and environment.

gates.workload: Input <= 64 KiB, one evaluation/replay process with bounded input count.
gates.acceptance: Measure process peak RSS externally; the Rust microbenchmark does not measure RSS.
gates.failure_policy: Investigate allocations and bounds; do not infer memory usage from latency.

gates.acceptance: Qualify at least two independently-shaped synthetic source adapters; every source field must be preserved, explicitly transformed by a named rule, or recorded as loss/unmapped. No silent field loss.
gates.failure_policy: Block federation until the semantic crosswalk and known-loss register are reviewed.

gates.acceptance: A separately implemented verifier reproduces all public vector outcomes and independently detects every envelope mutation in the shared fixture pack.
gates.failure_policy: No trust or release policy may rely on a single producer/verifier implementation.

gates.acceptance: No raw/high-rate telemetry, confidential process parameters, operator personal information or unauthorized tenant identifiers enter public receipts.
gates.failure_policy: Block integration and retain a test demonstrating the leakage path.

gates.acceptance: At least two Mycelix agents exercise publication, resolution, receipt verification, disputes, revocation observations and unauthorized-route negative controls under a qualified Holochain version.
gates.failure_policy: Unit tests alone do not establish DHT/bridge behavior.
